fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 does not specify the branching program, bent characters, hash-cover transitions, integer factor, target, weights, or coefficient bound. Expansion charges only nonzero mismatches; exact zero fingerprints from affine/parity combinations or signed accepting flows remain untouched by Z/A/P/S, while DROP, common radius, and two-level growth are unaudited.

Proposal 2's scalable premise is self-defeating: a uniformly constructible polynomial-size rational Macaulay system that is consistent for every satisfiable formula and inconsistent for every unsatisfiable formula would decide 3SAT by polynomial-time RREF. The proposed n=3, d=3 test uses the full Boolean degree and cannot discriminate whether any polynomial-size sparse schedule exists; conditional removal of Z/A/S does not address P or asymptotic size.

Proposal 3 has no emitted quadratic mechanism making the second skew singular value a distance penalty; decomposability and exterior rank risk becoming external nonlinear filters. Unrestricted integral forms retain A/P/S/T shortcuts, and the flags, contractions, Gram matrix, target, exact cosphericity, and adverse/legal recurrence are unspecified.

Proposal 4 specifies neither the truth-table lattice points nor the port embedding, center, normalization, free-sum gluing map, or exhaustive coefficient bound. A local empty Delaunay face does not imply closure under shared-port gluing: new zero-kernel, affine, parity, DROP, and signed-splice points can appear, so O/A/P/D/S/G remain unresolved.

Proposal 5 does not justify identifying Euclidean norms of integer multiplication-matrix coordinates with Minkowski-embedding energy. The product formula applies only after proving a fingerprint is nonzero, while G13-type affine unit relations can make it exactly zero; phase families, search domain, common sphere, DROP handling, and relative adverse/legal growth are unfrozen.

Proposal 6 leaves the Gram ansatz, normalization, SOS multipliers, margin, graph lift, factor, and target unspecified. Constant-degree integer-aware SOS does not itself escape affine/parity pseudodistributions, and the known additive two-copy parity remains a blocker unless an exact equal-radius term charges it; no two-level G inequality is defined.
evidence: No verifier, emitted CVP instance, exact center, control minimum, or complete shell certificate is supplied for any proposal. Their claimed experimental outcomes are unsupported.

G13 exhibited an exact harmful affine combination annihilating every compatible linear syndrome, and G15 lifted it through all hierarchy levels with zero residual. This directly obstructs the linear hash, Macaulay-lift, cyclotomic-tag, and SOS mechanisms unless they prove a nonlinear emitted escape.
G19 found a zero-residual accepting signed flow with two negative coefficients despite complete flow constraints. Proposal 1 gives no exact reason its hash cover cannot admit the same kind of splice.
G28 measured adverse growth below legal growth, while G32 found an exactly additive zero-residual parity witness of cost 432. No proposal supplies evidence overturning these growth blockers.

G30 showed that unrestricted integral coefficients defeat intended decomposable/rank-one tensor semantics. G33 and G34 separately failed exact common-sphere and positive-definite metric gates, directly warning against Proposals 3–5.

G12 found a cheaper clause-DROP vector, whereas G31 only passed one finite shell and yielded no composition law. Finite local separation therefore cannot be promoted to the requested polynomial approximation gap.
next_experiment: None is authorized. A resubmission must freeze one complete factor, target, control, common-radius certificate, coefficient bound, and two-level composition, then preregister an exhaustive shell containing exact kernels, G13/G15 affine lifts, parity copies, DROP, signed splices, and unrestricted entangled states with a direct lambda>mu test.
